q7.answer: The app keeps the three current key values and their version ids in an in-memory holder. The provider clients no longer copy the key in their constructors. Each call reads the current key from the holder, so a refresh takes effect on the next call without a restart. A refresh replaces the values only when all three reads succeed.

q8.answer: Two checks, after the rollout completes and after waiting at least one 5-minute refresh cycle plus a margin: every pod's latest logged version id must be the new one, and the provider's per-key usage must show zero use of the old key for the whole window. The margin length is still an open question (open question 5), and the check depends on each provider offering per-key usage reporting, which step 1 must confirm.

q9.answer: The order is: (1) inventory consumers and provider capabilities; (2) set up secret paths, KMS keys and IAM, including prod read for orders-api-prod and write for the security on-call only; (3) get dev keys; (4-8) write the loader, client changes, readiness gate, local dev setup and tests; (9) merge the code without deploying it; (10) rotate each key at its provider and then write the new value to the prod store; (11) verify that orders-api-prod can read the three paths; (16-17) merge the CI guard and remove the api_key lines from config/app.yaml, both before the rollout; (12) roll out the new image, which is when the app actually starts reading from the store; (13) confirm every instance is on the new version; (15) block rollback to pre-migration images; (14) revoke the old keys, provider by provider; (18-19) update docs and clean up local copies. Copying keys to the store happens in step 10, after the code merge in step 9 and before the rollout.

q10.answer: Local runs use dev-only keys from the dev secret path, orders-api/dev/<name>. The developer's dev-only identity reads them, and that identity can read orders-api/dev/* only, never the prod path. Local copies of config/app.yaml contain no keys. Until step 7 is done, local runs still use the live keys in the committed file, and step 19 has engineers delete any local copies of the live keys.

q11.answer: The instance logs an error and exits with a non-zero code, so the pod never becomes ready and the rollout halts while the old pods keep serving. The plan does not say whether the 3-retry sequence applies to a secret that is missing from a reachable store, or only to an unreachable store (step 2 mentions only unreachable). The startup text ("still missing after the retries") suggests retries apply, but that is not spelled out, so this detail is unsettled.
